title: Best Fish Tank Filter 2026: 5 on Planted and Reef
description: Best Fish Tank Filter 2026: 5 on Planted and Reef. Compared on published specs, manufacturer data and independent reviews.
lede: This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: Canister vs. hang-on-back vs. internal
paragraphs: Canister (Fluval FX6, Marineland Magniflow): sit outside tank, most media capacity. Best for 40+ gallons.
HOB power (AquaClear, Seachem Tidal): hang on tank rim, moderate capacity. Best for 20-75 gallons.
Internal (Tetra Whisper): submerged inside tank, smallest capacity. Best for under 40 gallons.

sections.heading: Actual vs. rated flow rate
paragraphs: Real-world flow is 60-80% of rated GPH (manufacturer ratings assume no head pressure).

Fluval FX6: 925 rated / 740 measured (80%). AquaClear 110: 500 rated / 425 (85%). Marineland Magniflow 360: 360 / 290 (81%). Tetra Whisper: 150 / 105 (70%). Seachem Tidal 110: 450 / 390 (87% — highest accuracy).

sections.heading: Best for each use
paragraphs: Best large tanks (75+ gal): Fluval FX6 ($420-490). The canister-filter benchmark.
Best HOB workhorse: AquaClear 110 ($85-110). Customizable media, standard hobby recommendation for decades.
Best mid-tier canister: Marineland Magniflow 360 ($140-180). Easier to clean than Fluval.
Best beginners: Tetra Whisper ($15-35). Submersible, easy setup, quiet.
Best HOB with skimmer: Seachem Tidal 110 ($130-170). Surface skimming, large media basket.

faqs.q: How big a filter do I need?
faqs.a: 4-6x tank volume per hour turnover. 75-gallon tank needs ~300-450 GPH actual flow. Heavily stocked needs 6-10x.

faqs.q: How often to clean filter media?
faqs.a: Mechanical: rinse in tank water every 2-4 weeks. Biological: rinse in tank water monthly (never tap water — chlorine kills bacteria). Chemical: replace every 4-6 weeks.
Yes — advanced aquarists run primary canister + secondary HOB for redundancy.

faqs.q: Canister worth the price over HOB?
faqs.a: For 40+ gallons or stocked tanks, yes — canisters have 3-5x media capacity of HOBs.

fluval-fx6-canister-filter.review: Fluval FX6 is the flagship large-tank canister. Rated 925 GPH (measured 740), 6L media capacity, self-priming, multi-stage filtration. Sits outside tank. Standard for 100-400 gallon tanks.

aquaclear-110-power-filter.review: AquaClear 110 has been the standard HOB recommendation for decades. Customizable media basket, flow control, 110-gallon capacity. Rated 500 GPH (measured 425).

marineland-magniflow-canister-filter.review: Marineland Magniflow 360 is the mid-tier canister filter. Rated 360 GPH (measured 290), 100-gallon capacity, quick-disconnect for easier maintenance than Fluval.

tetra-whisper-internal-filter.review: Tetra Whisper Internal is the right entry-level filter for 10-40 gallon tanks. Submersible, easy setup, quiet. Limited media customization (Tetra cartridges only).

seachem-tidal-110-power-filter.review: Seachem Tidal 110 is the right HOB with surface skimming. Removes protein films from water surface (useful for planted tanks). Large media basket, flow control. Rated 450 GPH (measured 390 — highest flow accuracy).
cons: More moving parts than basic HOBs

recommendedFor.label: Serious hobbyists with 100-gallon-plus reef or cichlid tanks
recommendedFor.reason: The FX6's 740 GPH actual flow and 6L media capacity handle high bioloads in large tanks that smaller filters can't sustain.

recommendedFor.label: DIY aquarists who swap custom filter media regularly
recommendedFor.reason: AquaClear's open media basket accepts any combination of foam, carbon, and bio-media — no proprietary cartridges required.

recommendedFor.label: Intermediate fishkeepers upgrading from a starter canister
recommendedFor.reason: The quick-disconnect valves make monthly maintenance far less messy than the Fluval, at roughly one-third of the price.

recommendedFor.label: First-time fish owners setting up a 10-40 gallon tank
recommendedFor.reason: At $15-35, fully submersible, and with a tool-free setup, it removes every barrier for someone buying their first aquarium.

recommendedFor.label: Planted-tank enthusiasts fighting surface film and oxygen loss
recommendedFor.reason: The built-in surface skimmer continuously pulls the protein film off the waterline, improving gas exchange and leaf clarity.
